answer_sql:
SELECT
  p.brand,
  d.country_name AS customer_country,
  SUM(s.net_amount) AS net_revenue
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
  ON s.product_key = p.product_key
JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
  ON s.customer_key = c.customer_key
JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS d
  ON c.country_code = d.country_code
WHERE
  s.order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
  AND s.order_date < CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
GROUP BY
  p.brand,
  d.country_name
ORDER BY
  p.brand ASC,
  net_revenue DESC

sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: How much money Contoso actually charged its customers, after discount, on orders placed during calendar year 2024 — split out for every pairing of one of the eleven brands it sells under with one of the eight countries its buyers live in. 88 rows, one per brand-and-country pair, no pair empty, together accounting for the entire 31,639,690.92 USD of that year with nothing dropped and nothing counted twice. Brands run alphabetically and within each brand the countries run from biggest earner down to smallest; every brand opens with the United States and closes with Italy. The largest single cell is Contoso bought by customers in the United States, 3,262,694.30; the smallest is Northwind Traders bought in Italy, 4,757.08. Sales through both channels are in it — walk-in shops and the web shop — and a web sale is placed by where the BUYER lives, not by any shop's location. Figures are rounded to cents from the five-decimal values the query returned. WHAT THE FIGURE DOES NOT INCLUDE: no deduction for returns, tax or shipping, because this bundle holds no such columns — net means gross less discount and no more; the year is the calendar year, not a fiscal one; and sales are dated by when the order was placed, not when it was delivered.

turns.why: Render the final answer — all 88 brand-and-country rows in their settled order — serialized into one row so that every value is readable in full rather than truncated, together with the row count and total as a last reconciliation against step 2.
turns.did:
WITH pairs AS (
  SELECT
    p.brand,
    d.country_name,
    SUM(s.net_amount) AS net_revenue
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
    ON s.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
    ON s.customer_key = c.customer_key
  JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS d
    ON c.country_code = d.country_code
  WHERE
    s.order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
    AND s.order_date < CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
  GROUP BY
    p.brand,
    d.country_name
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS rows_returned,
  ROUND(SUM(net_revenue), 2) AS total_check,
  LISTAGG(
    brand || '~' || country_name || '~' || CAST(ROUND(net_revenue, 2) AS TEXT), ' ; '
    ORDER BY
      brand ASC,
      net_revenue DESC
  ) AS answer_table
FROM pairs
